238	def metrics(T, keep, rows, tag, controls=True, draws=CONTROL_DRAWS):
239	    """Kept-vs-skipped metrics of a boolean keep mask over the rows `rows` of T (a subset of one split)."""
240	    keep = np.asarray(keep, dtype=bool)
241	    k = rows[keep[rows]]; s = rows[~keep[rows]]
242	    net, win = T.net, T.win
243	    nk, ns = len(k), len(s)
244	    m = dict(n=int(len(rows)), kept_n=int(nk), skipped_n=int(ns), kept_share=round(nk / len(rows), 4) if len(rows) else None,
245	             kept_net=round(float(net[k].sum()), 2), skipped_net=round(float(net[s].sum()), 2),
246	             kept_mean=round(float(net[k].mean()), 2) if nk else None, skipped_mean=round(float(net[s].mean()), 2) if ns else None,
247	             all_mean=round(float(net[rows].mean()), 2) if len(rows) else None,
248	             kept_win_rate=round(float(win[k].mean()), 4) if nk else None, skipped_win_rate=round(float(win[s].mean()), 4) if ns else None,
249	             kept_pf=None, kept_t=None, diff=None, diff_top1_removed=None, kept_mean_slip3=None, kept_mean_slip8=None,
250	             loser_recall=None, loser_precision=None, winner_recall=None, winner_recall_weighted=None, top_decile_winners_skipped=None,
251	             kept_sessions=int(len(set(T.session[k].tolist()))), sign_blocks=None, perm_p=None, control_pct=None, control_p_beat=None)
252	    if nk:
253	        w_, l_ = net[k][net[k] > 0], net[k][net[k] <= 0]
254	        m["kept_pf"] = round(float(w_.sum() / -l_.sum()), 3) if len(l_) and l_.sum() else None
255	        m["kept_t"] = round(float(net[k].mean() / (net[k].std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(nk))), 2) if nk > 1 and net[k].std(ddof=1) else None
256	    if nk and ns:
257	        m["diff"] = round(float(net[k].mean() - net[s].mean()), 2)
258	        # slippage moves every trade's net by the same amount, so the kept-vs-skipped difference is invariant; what a marginal
259	        # gate must survive is the kept book's own expectancy at 3 / 8 pts per side
260	        for sl_ in (3.0, 8.0): m[f"kept_mean_slip{int(sl_)}"] = round(float(T.net_slip[sl_][k].mean()), 2)
261	        top = np.quantile(net[rows], 0.99); kk, ss_ = k[net[k] < top], s[net[s] < top]
262	        m["diff_top1_removed"] = round(float(net[kk].mean() - net[ss_].mean()), 2) if len(kk) and len(ss_) else None
263	        L = ~win[rows]; W = win[rows]
264	        skp = ~keep[rows]
265	        m["loser_recall"] = round(float((skp & L).sum() / L.sum()), 4) if L.sum() else None
266	        m["loser_precision"] = round(float((skp & L).sum() / skp.sum()), 4) if skp.sum() else None
267	        m["winner_recall"] = round(float((~skp & W).sum() / W.sum()), 4) if W.sum() else None
268	        wn = net[rows]
269	        m["winner_recall_weighted"] = round(float(wn[~skp & W].sum() / wn[W].sum()), 4) if W.sum() and wn[W].sum() else None
270	        if W.sum():
271	            q = np.quantile(wn[W], 0.9); big = W & (wn >= q)
272	            m["top_decile_winners_skipped"] = round(float((skp & big).sum() / big.sum()), 4) if big.sum() else None
273	        bl = T.block[rows]
274	        if (bl >= 0).all():
275	            m["sign_blocks"] = int(sum(1 for b in range(N_BLOCKS) if (keep[rows] & (bl == b)).sum() and (~keep[rows] & (bl == b)).sum()
276	                                      and net[rows][keep[rows] & (bl == b)].mean() > net[rows][~keep[rows] & (bl == b)].mean()))
277	        if controls:
278	            pp = fz_report.permutation_p(net[k].tolist(), net[s].tolist(), draws, SEED, tag)
279	            m["perm_p"] = pp["p"]
280	            rc = fz_report.random_control(_units(T, rows), _units(T, k, "SEL"), draws, SEED, tag)
281	            m["control_pct"], m["control_p_beat"], m["control_p50"] = rc["fz_pct"], rc["p_beat"], rc["p50"]
282	    return m

285	def session_vectors(T, keep, rows):
286	    """Per active session (sessions with a unit among rows): kept sum / n, skipped sum / n, all sum / n."""
287	    keep = np.asarray(keep, dtype=bool)
288	    ses = T.session[rows]; net = T.net[rows]; kp = keep[rows]
289	    S = np.array(sorted(set(ses.tolist())))
290	    idx = np.searchsorted(S, ses)
291	    out = {}
292	    for name, msk in (("kept", kp), ("skipped", ~kp), ("all", np.ones(len(rows), dtype=bool))):
293	        out[name + "_sum"] = np.bincount(idx, weights=net * msk, minlength=len(S))
294	        out[name + "_n"] = np.bincount(idx, weights=msk.astype(float), minlength=len(S))
295	    out["sessions"] = S
296	    return out

357	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- multiplicity: CSCV / PBO, deflated Sharpe, effective trials
358	def _partitions(S=CSCV_S):
359	    """All C(S, S/2) IS / pseudo-OOS block assignments as a boolean matrix (partitions x S), True = in-sample half."""
360	    combs = list(itertools.combinations(range(S), S // 2))
361	    M = np.zeros((len(combs), S), dtype=bool)
362	    for i, cmb in enumerate(combs): M[i, list(cmb)] = True
363	    return M

366	def pbo(vectors, statistic="kept_mean", S=CSCV_S):
367	    """CSCV probability of backtest overfitting (Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado & Zhu 2017) over a family of candidates.
368	    vectors: list of session_vectors dicts (one per candidate, same sessions). Each candidate's per-session series is split into
369	    S contiguous blocks; for every C(S, S/2) partition the IS-best candidate's OOS rank is recorded; PBO = share of partitions
370	    where that rank is below the median (logit < 0). statistic: 'kept_mean' = kept net per kept trade over the half, or 'diff'
371	    = kept mean minus skipped mean over the half. Also the IS-vs-OOS performance degradation slope and the share of partitions
372	    where the IS-best is below zero OOS."""
373	    M = len(vectors)
374	    if M < 2: return dict(candidates=M, pbo=None, note="needs at least 2 candidates")
375	    T_ = len(vectors[0]["sessions"]); edges = np.linspace(0, T_, S + 1).round().astype(int)
376	    def blocks(v, key):
377	        return np.array([v[key][edges[b]:edges[b + 1]].sum() for b in range(S)])
378	    KS = np.array([blocks(v, "kept_sum") for v in vectors]); KN = np.array([blocks(v, "kept_n") for v in vectors])
379	    SS = np.array([blocks(v, "skipped_sum") for v in vectors]); SN = np.array([blocks(v, "skipped_n") for v in vectors])
380	    P = _partitions(S).astype(float)                                           # partitions x S
381	    def perf(Pm):
382	        ks, kn = Pm @ KS.T, Pm @ KN.T                                           # partitions x M
383	        with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
384	            km = np.where(kn > 0, ks / kn, np.nan)
385	            if statistic == "kept_mean": return km
386	            ss, sn = Pm @ SS.T, Pm @ SN.T
387	            return km - np.where(sn > 0, ss / sn, np.nan)
388	    ins, oos = perf(P), perf(1 - P)
389	    ins = np.where(np.isnan(ins), -np.inf, ins)
390	    best = np.argmax(ins, axis=1)
391	    oos_best = oos[np.arange(len(P)), best]
392	    ranks = np.array([(np.nan_to_num(oos[i], nan=-np.inf) < oos_best[i]).sum() / (M - 1) if M > 1 else 0.5 for i in range(len(P))])
393	    ranks = np.clip(ranks, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)
394	    logit = np.log(ranks / (1 - ranks))
395	    ins_best = ins[np.arange(len(P)), best]
396	    ok = np.isfinite(oos_best) & np.isfinite(ins_best)
397	    slope = float(np.polyfit(ins_best[ok], oos_best[ok], 1)[0]) if ok.sum() > 2 else None
398	    return dict(candidates=M, partitions=int(len(P)), statistic=statistic, pbo=round(float((logit < 0).mean()), 4),
399	                oos_best_below_zero=round(float((oos_best[ok] < 0).mean()), 4) if ok.any() else None,
400	                degradation_slope=round(slope, 4) if slope is not None else None,
401	                is_best_mean=round(float(ins_best[ok].mean()), 2) if ok.any() else None,
402	                oos_best_mean=round(float(oos_best[ok].mean()), 2) if ok.any() else None)
403

405	def effective_trials(vectors, key="kept_sum"):
406	    """Participation-ratio count of independent trials from the correlation matrix of the candidates' per-session series."""
407	    X = np.array([v[key] for v in vectors], dtype=float)
408	    X = X[:, X.std(axis=0) > 0] if X.shape[0] > 1 else X
409	    if X.shape[0] < 2: return float(X.shape[0])
410	    C = np.corrcoef(X); C = np.nan_to_num(C, nan=0.0); np.fill_diagonal(C, 1.0)
411	    lam = np.clip(np.linalg.eigvalsh(C), 0, None)
412	    return round(float(lam.sum() ** 2 / (lam ** 2).sum()), 2)

415	def deflated_sharpe(per_session, n_trials, sr_var_trials=None):
416	    """Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2014): the probability that the per-session Sharpe of a book is above the expected maximum
417	    Sharpe of n_trials trials with variance sr_var_trials (the variance of Sharpe across the family; estimated from
418	    per_session's own scale when None), with the skew / kurtosis correction. Returns SR, SR0, DSR, p = 1 - DSR."""
419	    x = np.asarray(per_session, dtype=float); T_ = len(x)
420	    if T_ < 3 or x.std(ddof=1) == 0: return dict(sr=None, sr0=None, dsr=None, p=None, T=T_)
421	    sr = float(x.mean() / x.std(ddof=1)); g3 = float(sst.skew(x)); g4 = float(sst.kurtosis(x, fisher=False))
422	    V = sr_var_trials if sr_var_trials is not None else 1.0 / T_
423	    N = max(2, n_trials); em = 0.5772156649
424	    sr0 = math.sqrt(V) * ((1 - em) * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / N) + em * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / (N * math.e)))
425	    den = 1 - g3 * sr + (g4 - 1) / 4 * sr * sr
426	    if den <= 0: return dict(sr=round(sr, 4), sr0=round(sr0, 4), dsr=None, p=None, T=T_, note="denominator <= 0")
427	    z = (sr - sr0) * math.sqrt(T_ - 1) / math.sqrt(den)
428	    dsr = float(sst.norm.cdf(z))
429	    return dict(sr=round(sr, 4), sr0=round(float(sr0), 4), dsr=round(dsr, 4), p=round(1 - dsr, 4), T=T_, n_trials=n_trials, skew=round(g3, 3), kurt=round(g4, 3))

432	def min_backtest_length(sr, n_trials, sr_var_trials):
433	    """Sessions needed for the observed per-session Sharpe to clear the expected maximum of n_trials (AFML 14.7)."""
434	    N = max(2, n_trials); em = 0.5772156649
435	    sr0 = math.sqrt(sr_var_trials) * ((1 - em) * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / N) + em * sst.norm.ppf(1 - 1 / (N * math.e)))
436	    return round(float((sr0 / sr) ** 2 + 1), 1) if sr > 0 else None

439	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- resampling: stationary block bootstrap of sessions, SPA
440	def stationary_bootstrap_idx(T_, draws=BOOT_DRAWS, mean_block=BOOT_MEAN_BLOCK, seed=SEED, tag=""):
441	    """Politis & Romano stationary bootstrap indices (draws x T_) over T_ ordered sessions; seeded and reproducible."""
442	    rng = np.random.default_rng(int(_sha(f"{seed}|boot|{tag}"), 16) % (2 ** 32))
443	    p = 1.0 / mean_block
444	    starts = rng.integers(0, T_, size=(draws, T_)); cont = rng.random((draws, T_)) >= p
445	    idx = np.empty((draws, T_), dtype=int)
446	    idx[:, 0] = starts[:, 0]
447	    for t_ in range(1, T_):
448	        idx[:, t_] = np.where(cont[:, t_], (idx[:, t_ - 1] + 1) % T_, starts[:, t_])
449	    return idx
450	
451	
452	def bootstrap_ci(vec, draws=BOOT_DRAWS, ci=GO["boot_ci"], tag=""):
453	    """Block-bootstrap CI (sessions resampled) of the kept-vs-skipped difference and of the kept mean from a session_vectors dict."""
454	    T_ = len(vec["sessions"]); idx = stationary_bootstrap_idx(T_, draws, tag=tag)
455	    ks, kn, ss, sn = (vec[k][idx].sum(axis=1) for k in ("kept_sum", "kept_n", "skipped_sum", "skipped_n"))
456	    with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
457	        km = np.where(kn > 0, ks / kn, np.nan); sm = np.where(sn > 0, ss / sn, np.nan); d = km - sm
458	    a = (1 - ci) / 2
459	    q = lambda v: [round(float(np.nanquantile(v, a)), 2), round(float(np.nanquantile(v, 1 - a)), 2)]
460	    return dict(draws=draws, ci=ci, diff_ci=q(d), kept_mean_ci=q(km), diff_p_le0=round(float(np.nanmean(d <= 0)), 4),
461	                diff_point=round(float(np.nansum(vec["kept_sum"]) / max(1, vec["kept_n"].sum()) - np.nansum(vec["skipped_sum"]) / max(1, vec["skipped_n"].sum())), 2))
462	
463	
464	def selection_gain(vec):
465	    """Per-session selection gain d_t = kept mean in session t minus the session's mean over all units (0 when nothing kept):
466	    the per-session statistic behind the session-matched random control (its expectation under random selection is 0)."""
467	    with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
468	        km = np.where(vec["kept_n"] > 0, vec["kept_sum"] / vec["kept_n"], np.nan)
469	        am = vec["all_sum"] / vec["all_n"]
470	    d = km - am
471	    return np.where(np.isnan(d), 0.0, d), vec["kept_n"] > 0
472	
473	
474	SPA_ACTIVE_TOL_INR = 0.01   # a session counts as "active" for a candidate only if its selection gain exceeds this many INR
475	                            # (the labels are priced to 2 dp; lab.manage replays carry ~1e-3 INR of float noise against them,
476	                            # which a 1e-9 test counted as activity: the exit-policy follow-up refuter's finding, 2026-09-29)
477	
478	
479	def spa(vectors, draws=BOOT_DRAWS, tag="", min_active=None, active_tol=SPA_ACTIVE_TOL_INR):
480	    """White's Reality Check and Hansen's SPA over a family of candidates: H0 = no candidate has positive expected selection
481	    gain (per-session kept mean minus the session mean). Stationary bootstrap of sessions, Hansen's consistent recentring;
482	    reported both studentised (Hansen) and unstudentised (White's original statistic, sqrt(T) x mean). A candidate whose
483	    selection gain differs from zero (by more than `active_tol` INR, default SPA_ACTIVE_TOL_INR = 0.01) in fewer than
484	    `min_active` sessions (default max(10, 5% of T)) is excluded from the studentised family: its near-zero variance would give
485	    it an arbitrarily large t (the exit-policy refuter's finding); it stays in the unstudentised family. Gate candidates (keep
486	    masks) are unaffected by the tolerance: their per-session gains are exactly 0 or hundreds of INR. Returns the best
487	    candidate under each statistic and the four p-values."""
488	    Dm = np.array([selection_gain(v)[0] for v in vectors], dtype=float)       # M x T
489	    M, T_ = Dm.shape
490	    if min_active is None: min_active = max(10, int(0.05 * T_))
491	    active = (np.abs(Dm) > active_tol).sum(axis=1)
492	    ok = active >= min_active
493	    mu = Dm.mean(axis=1); sd = Dm.std(axis=1, ddof=1) + 1e-12
494	    idx = stationary_bootstrap_idx(T_, draws, tag=tag)
495	    mub = np.stack([Dm[:, idx[d]].mean(axis=1) for d in range(draws)])           # draws x M
496	    sdb = np.stack([Dm[:, idx[d]].std(axis=1, ddof=1) for d in range(draws)]) + 1e-12
497	    thr = np.sqrt(np.var(Dm, axis=1, ddof=1) / T_ * 2 * math.log(math.log(T_)))
498	    mu_c = np.where(mu < -thr, mu, 0.0)                                            # Hansen's consistent recentring
499	    out = dict(candidates=M, sessions=T_, draws=draws, min_active_sessions=int(min_active), excluded_from_studentised=int((~ok).sum()))
500	    # unstudentised (White 2000): statistic sqrt(T) x mean gain, every candidate
501	    tu = np.sqrt(T_) * mu; bu = int(np.argmax(tu)); stat_u = float(tu[bu])
502	    rc_u = np.max(np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu), axis=1); spa_u = np.max(np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu + mu_c), axis=1)
503	    out.update(best_unstudentised=bu, best_mean_gain_unstudentised=round(float(mu[bu]), 2),
504	               rc_p_unstudentised=round(float((rc_u >= stat_u).mean()), 4), spa_p_unstudentised=round(float((spa_u >= stat_u).mean()), 4))
505	    # studentised (Hansen 2005), candidates with enough active sessions
506	    if ok.any():
507	        ts = np.where(ok, np.sqrt(T_) * mu / sd, -np.inf); bs = int(np.argmax(ts)); stat_s = float(ts[bs])
508	        rc_s = np.max(np.where(ok, np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu) / sdb, -np.inf), axis=1)
509	        spa_s = np.max(np.where(ok, np.sqrt(T_) * (mub - mu + mu_c) / sdb, -np.inf), axis=1)
510	        out.update(best=bs, best_mean_gain=round(float(mu[bs]), 2), best_t=round(stat_s, 3), best_active_sessions=int(active[bs]),
511	                   rc_p=round(float((rc_s >= stat_s).mean()), 4), spa_p=round(float((spa_s >= stat_s).mean()), 4))
512	    else:
513	        out.update(best=None, best_mean_gain=None, best_t=None, best_active_sessions=None, rc_p=None, spa_p=None)
514	    return out
515

517	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- structural breaks of the book's own expectancy
518	def _hac_var(x, lag=5):
519	    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float) - np.mean(x); T_ = len(x)
520	    s = float((x * x).sum())
521	    for k in range(1, lag + 1):
522	        w = 1 - k / (lag + 1); s += 2 * w * float((x[k:] * x[:-k]).sum())
523	    return s / T_ / T_                                                             # variance of the mean
524	
525	
526	def chow_mean(x, y, lag=5):
527	    """HAC (Newey-West, Bartlett, lag 5) t-test of a difference of means between two consecutive segments."""
528	    x, y = np.asarray(x, dtype=float), np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
529	    if len(x) < 5 or len(y) < 5: return dict(t=None, p=None, n=[len(x), len(y)])
530	    t_ = (y.mean() - x.mean()) / math.sqrt(_hac_var(x, lag) + _hac_var(y, lag))
531	    return dict(t=round(float(t_), 3), p=round(float(2 * (1 - sst.norm.cdf(abs(t_)))), 4), mean_before=round(float(x.mean()), 2),
532	                mean_after=round(float(y.mean()), 2), n=[len(x), len(y)])
533	
534	
535	def bde_cusum(x, k=10):
536	    """Brown-Durbin-Evans CUSUM of recursive residuals of the constant-mean model on the ordered series x: the maximum
537	    crossing of the 5% bands +-0.948 sqrt(T-k) (1 + 2 (r-k)/(T-k)); reports whether the path leaves the band and where."""
538	    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float); T_ = len(x)
539	    if T_ <= k + 2: return dict(break_detected=None)
540	    w = np.array([(x[t_] - x[:t_].mean()) / math.sqrt(1 + 1 / t_) for t_ in range(k, T_)])
541	    sig = w.std(ddof=1)
542	    W = np.cumsum(w) / sig
543	    r = np.arange(k + 1, T_ + 1)
544	    band = 0.948 * math.sqrt(T_ - k) * (1 + 2 * (r - k) / (T_ - k))
545	    ex = np.abs(W) > band
546	    return dict(break_detected=bool(ex.any()), first_crossing_index=int(np.argmax(ex)) + k if ex.any() else None,
547	                max_ratio=round(float(np.max(np.abs(W) / band)), 3), T=T_)
548

550	def break_tests(T, lag=5):
551	    """The pre-registration step: has the book's per-session expectancy (active sessions, label L1) changed inside IS or at the
552	    IS / OOS boundary? Rolling 60-session mean with block-bootstrap bands, BDE CUSUM, HAC Chow tests per calendar year, and the
553	    one permitted OOS aggregate read: the Chow test at 2026-01-01 (it decides the OOS caveat, never a key)."""
554	    rows = np.arange(T.n)
555	    ses = T.session[rows]; net = T.net[rows]
556	    S = np.array(sorted(set(ses.tolist()))); idx = np.searchsorted(S, ses)
557	    per = np.bincount(idx, weights=net, minlength=len(S)) / np.bincount(idx, minlength=len(S))
558	    day = dict(zip(T.session, T.day)); days = np.array([day[int(s)] for s in S])
559	    is_ = days <= IS_END
560	    x_is = per[is_]
561	    years = sorted({d[:4] for d in days[is_]})
562	    chow_years = {}
563	    for y in years[1:]:
564	        before = x_is[np.array([d[:4] < y for d in days[is_]])]; after = x_is[np.array([d[:4] == y for d in days[is_]])]
565	        chow_years[y] = chow_mean(before, after, lag)
566	    boundary = chow_mean(x_is, per[~is_], lag)
567	    roll = pd.Series(x_is).rolling(60).mean().to_numpy()
568	    idxb = stationary_bootstrap_idx(len(x_is), 500, tag="roll")
569	    rb = np.array([pd.Series(x_is[idxb[d]]).rolling(60).mean().to_numpy() for d in range(500)])
570	    lo, hi = np.nanquantile(rb, 0.05, axis=0), np.nanquantile(rb, 0.95, axis=0)
571	    outside = int(np.nansum((roll < lo) | (roll > hi)))
572	    return dict(label=T.label, active_is_sessions=int(is_.sum()), is_mean_per_session=round(float(x_is.mean()), 2),
573	                bde=bde_cusum(x_is), chow_per_year=chow_years, chow_is_oos_boundary=boundary,
574	                rolling60_outside_band=outside, rolling60_points=int(np.isfinite(roll).sum()),
575	                winners_only_boundary=chow_mean(x_is[x_is > 0], per[~is_][per[~is_] > 0], lag) if (per[~is_] > 0).sum() >= 5 else None,
576	                caveat=("IS/OOS boundary Chow p < 0.05: the OOS window is not from the same process; every OOS table carries this"
577	                        if boundary["p"] is not None and boundary["p"] < 0.05 else "no boundary break at 5%"))

606	    ch["control_pct>=95"] = (res.get("control_pct") is not None and res["control_pct"] >= GO["control_pct_min"], res.get("control_pct"))
607	    if cpcv is not None: ch["cpcv_p5_diff>0"] = (cpcv.get("diff_p5") is not None and cpcv["diff_p5"] > GO["cpcv_p5_diff_min"], cpcv.get("diff_p5"))

614	    else:

# importance: FINDINGS (DESIGN_PANEL quant-ml-canon-feature-importance, both judges' fixes)

**What this study is.** The feature-vocabulary pass: which clusters of as-of columns (base design + the 61 extended columns handed here by the regime-breaks, regime-states, motif-shapelet and rocket-probe judges) carry information about the L1 outcome under the harness splitter; the shortlist of at most 8 clusters per timeframe that the gate studies may draw features from, frozen in the ledger before the phase-3 gate studies (gate_family, llm_round1, regime_gate; the H1-H5, session_stop, llm round 0, rocket and exit_policy searches preceded it and were not restricted to it: 'Repair', issue 1, and the `correction` records in `ledger/registrations.jsonl`); the FFD verdict; the five interaction pairs that are the only depth-2/3 conjunctions allowed downstream. This study proposes **no gate**: the only kept-vs-skipped numbers are the ledger rows of the OOF gates it had to evaluate (the full bagged model at its training-fold tau, each SFI cluster at its tau, the CPCV paths of the full model), reported as ceilings, never as candidates. IS only.

## Definitions (fixed before the numbers)

```
Importance study library (DESIGN_PANEL: quant-ml-canon-feature-importance, both judges' fixes; feature hand-offs from
regime-breaks, regime-states, motif-shapelet, rocket-probe). Every definition below is fixed before any number is looked at.

Feature set        harness.design(T) (base as-of columns, one-hot text, 0/1 booleans) + the 61 extended as-of columns of
                   features_ext/<tf>/ext_features.parquet joined on setup_i. Columns with > 40% NaN on IS rows dropped and listed;
                   constant columns dropped; exact duplicates (|Spearman| > 0.999 on IS) dropped, the first kept; of a two-level
                   one-hot the second level is dropped (its complement carries the same information). Missing indicators
                   `<col>__na` for every kept column with a NaN on IS, de-duplicated by NaN pattern (one indicator per pattern,
                   named after its first column; the covered columns are listed). Median imputation uses the TRAINING fold's
                   medians (bagging); xgboost sees NaN as such.
Label / weights    L1 binary (net > 0); sample weight = |net| winsorised at the training fold's 99th percentile, normalised to
                   mean 1; class balance by DecisionTreeClassifier(class_weight="balanced"). Test-fold weights for the weighted
                   log-loss: |net| of the test rows winsorised at the SAME training-fold p99, normalised to mean 1 on the fold.
Model              BaggingClassifier(DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=4 (3 and 5 as a sensitivity), min_weight_fraction_leaf=0.05,
                   class_weight="balanced"), n_estimators=300, bootstrap, oob_score) under harness.purged_splits (12 blocks).
tau                chosen INSIDE the training fold on the bagging's out-of-bag probabilities: the p_win threshold on the grid
                   0.05..0.95 (step 0.01) maximising the kept mean net subject to |net|-weighted winner recall >= 0.90.
Clustering         Spearman correlation on IS rows (pairwise-complete; undefined -> 0), distance sqrt(0.5 (1 - rho)), scipy
                   average linkage, the cut with the best silhouette (precomputed distance) over 20..40 clusters.
Representative     per cluster, by config-expressibility tier (0 = integer-valued / boolean / one-hot / card or fz field;
                   1 = ATR ratio or other dimensionless; 2 = raw points / levels), then coverage, then centrality (mean |rho| to
                   the cluster's members).
Clustered MDA      per fold, the features of a cluster are permuted JOINTLY on the test rows (same row permutation for every
                   member, missing indicators included), 5 permutations; recorded per fold: the increase in OOF weighted log-loss
                   (primary: the pass rule and the ranks) and the decrease in the OOF kept-vs-skipped mean-net difference at the
                   fold's tau (harness.metrics, controls off; secondary, reported with its own ratio). Mean and std across the 12
                   folds; a cluster passes MDA when mean > std (log-loss).
MDI                per fold forest: sum over trees of feature_importances_ / n_trees, summed per cluster, averaged over folds.
SFI                each cluster alone (its members + indicators), same folds, same weights, same tau rule; its OOF gate is a
                   ledger row (family importance/sfi).
Stability          the per-fold, per-permutation OOF probabilities are kept per row, so the log-loss MDA is re-computed on the
                   rows of each period (minute: calendar years 2022 (with 2021-10..12), 2023, 2024, 2025; 5minute: halves
                   2021-10..2023-09 and 2023-10..2025-12); a cluster ranks top-8 in >= 3 of 4 years (minute) / in both halves
                   (5minute) or it is not shortlisted. The models are the 12 fold models (trained on the other 11 purged blocks).
Orthogonal check   PCA on the standardised (IS-median-imputed, z-scored) IS features; a bagging of the same shape on the PC
                   scores; scipy.stats.weightedtau between its MDI per component and the eigenvalues.
Interactions       xgboost max_depth 3, 200 rounds, eta 0.05, the same folds, on the top-40 features by clustered MDA (clusters
                   in MDA order, members in MDI order); shap.TreeExplainer(...).shap_interaction_values on the OOF rows; pairs
                   ranked by mean |interaction|; the top 5 pairs carry the gain-weighted median split point of each feature over
                   the tree paths where both features occur (all 12 fold boosters pooled).
```

Constants: trees 300, min_weight_fraction_leaf 0.05, main depth 4 (sensitivity (3, 5)), permutations per fold 5, tau grid 0.05..0.95 step 0.01, weighted winner recall floor 0.9, silhouette range 20..40 clusters, stability top-8, interactions on the top-40 features, 5 pairs; xgboost depth 3, 200 rounds, eta 0.05. # exit_policy — FINDINGS (IS only, 2026-09-29)

Study `decision-making-2-exit-policy-fqi-exomdp` (DESIGN_PANEL, both judges' fixes) with BRIEF addendum 6: the managed replay is `lab.manage` / `lab.price_trade`, never a second implementation. Entries are frozen (every IS unit of `harness.load(tf)`, label L1, both timeframes); only the exit changes. No OOS row was read.

## 1. Definitions (fixed before the numbers)

- **Entries**: the L1 units, entry at the SETUP bar's close in the SETUP's direction; 1 min = Strategy 1 rules (prev_swing stop), 5 min = Strategy 2 rules (choch_candle stop).
- **Square-off bar**: the last bar of the entry session opening at or before 15:25 (`lab.eod_cut`); **cap** = min(square-off bar, the contract's last candle) — every comparator is cut there.
- **Foundation stop**: `features.sl`, engine touch convention (open beyond the stop -> fill at the open; wick touch -> fill at the stop; a session's first bar -> the close). Identical to `lab.manage`'s stop (proved on every IS trade, section 2).
- **Extended trajectory** (learners A / B, the floor oracle): bars entry+1 .. J_end, J_end = the Foundation stop bar when it fires before the cap, else the cap. Exits before J_end are at the bar's close; at J_end the exit is the stop fill or the cap close. The engine's next-CHoCH exit is not applied (Exo-MDP: the tape does not react, so every exit policy is replayable).
- **Value**: net INR per trade per lot = `lab.price_trade` arithmetic (lot 65, 5 pts slippage per side, `lab.trade_charges(ZERODHA_NFO_FUT)` on the slipped prices); a 3-lot ladder is reported per position and per lot (position net / 3); selection and every comparison use per lot.
- **Oracle (free)**: the best close exit over entry+1 .. cap with no stop (an upper bound for any close-exit policy; a target filled intrabar can exceed it by at most that bar's range). **Oracle (floor)**: the best exit on the extended trajectory, ties -> earliest (learner B's target). **Exit regret** = oracle - policy.
- **Random-exit control**: exit at a uniformly drawn bar of entry+1 .. cap at its close, 2,000 seeded draws (`fz|exit`); a policy's percentile = share of draws whose mean net per lot is below the policy's (+ half the ties).
- **CHoCH against**: an `events.parquet` CHoCH with i > entry, i <= t, direction opposite to the position (known at its own bar under touch rules). **Time stop N**: exit at the close of bar entry+N if still open.
- **Cut convention (learner C)**: the time stop and the CHoCH-against exit are a post-processing cut of `lab.manage`'s tranches: every tranche whose lab exit bar is later than the cut bar exits at the cut bar's close instead; a tranche the lab closed at or before the cut bar keeps its exit (the stop / target on the cut bar is assumed first, as `lab.manage` assumes the stop first on a candle); with both cuts on, the earlier bar wins.
- **Learner C grid** (never shrunk): stop {35, 50, 75 pts, Foundation stop via `exact_R`} x scale_out {none, 1R, 2R, 3R, 4R with 1 lot (the target is the exit), ladder 1R/2R, ladder 2R/4R with 3 lots} x trail {none, (2,1), (2,2), (3,1), (3,2), (4,1), (4,2)} x time stop {none, 30, 60, 120 bars} x CHoCH-against {off, on}; square_off 15:25 always: 196 `lab.manage` positions x 8 cuts = **1,568 variants per timeframe**, each a strategy-row dict as `rl.py` builds it (lot 65, slippage 5, `position_json`, cap = the contract's last candle as `rl.contract_end`).
- **Selection (C)**: nested in `harness.purged_splits` (argmax of the training fold's mean net per lot, applied to the test fold) and in the 66 CPCV splits -> 11 paths (`harness.cpcv_paths`). **Learners A / B**: 3 contiguous session-block folds (harness blocks 0-3 / 4-7 / 8-11), purge of training trades whose trajectory intersects the test fold's bars, 3-session embargo; B's p* by an inner 3-fold on the training fold; A's Q-ensembles refit per fold.
- **Multiplicity**: every variant and every learner is a row of the append-only `exit_ledger.jsonl` + `vectors/*.npz` (harness-compatible per-session vectors: kept = the variant, skipped / all = the Foundation L1 exit on the same entries, so `harness.pbo(vecs, 'diff')`, `harness.spa`, `harness.effective_trials`, `harness.bootstrap_ci` read them unchanged). The harness ledger (`OUT/ledger/`) is for gates; this study writes to it only the gate x exit rows of section 8.
- **Pass rule** for an exit candidate (adapted from `harness.GO` to a policy-vs-Foundation difference on frozen entries): nested-CV diff > 0; CPCV 5th percentile diff > 0; random-exit percentile >= 95; 12-block sign-flip one-sided p <= 0.05 with >= 8 blocks positive; **lower bound of the 90% block-bootstrap CI of the diff > 0** (`boot_ci90_lower>0`, as `harness.go_no_go` implements it: a CI entirely below 0 fails; the earlier wording 'CI excludes 0' was loose — repair, section 11); **diff with the top 1% winners removed > 0** (the harness's pre-registered `diff_top1_removed` item: the trades whose policy net is in its own top 1% are dropped, the paired diff is averaged over the rest — `diff_top1_winners_removed` in `eval_table_*.csv`); PBO <= 0.2; studentised SPA p <= 0.10 over the family (the family's vectors at the label's 2-dp precision — repair, section 11). **Disclosure (repair)**: the earlier text of this rule read 'diff with the top 1% of per-trade *gains* removed > 0' (`diff_top1_gains_removed`: the trades whose gain over the Foundation exit is in the top 1% are dropped). That variant was written after learner C's results had been read (this script's own docstring) and is negative-biased by construction: removing the top 1% of a dispersed difference lowers its mean even when the true mean is zero (its zero-mean reference, the same trim on the centred difference, is about -150 INR on 1 min). It is reported beside the pass item with that reference and is not used to decide.

**No session memory beyond the hour effect is shown, and no `session_stop` key is proposed for ST13/ST14.** The as-run pre-registered null N1 (outcomes permuted within session x hour_bin cells over fixed positions) was rejected on 1 min (all seven tests, Holm p <= 0.0140) with a positive excess of +53 to +106 INR/trade, which the as-run study read as mean-reverting session memory. **That rejection is an artifact** (section R.1): the SETUP positions are generated by the outcomes (a trade runs until exit, winners hold ~6x longer than losers), and a memoryless generator that keeps only the clock and the durations reproduces the rejection on 100% of its streams (excess +84 to +119; 6% when the duration is made independent of the outcome). Two hindsight-free nulls replace it (section R.2): the within-hour contrast across sessions with a session-block bootstrap (N4) and the observed statistics against 2,000 memoryless streams (N3); on 1 min the min Holm p is N4 1.0000 / N3 1.0000, on 5 min N4 0.4198 / N3 0.0070: 1 min **NOT REJECTED under N3 or N4**; 5 min **INCONCLUSIVE: exactly one hindsight-free null rejects (or signs disagree)** (N3 alone rejects on `stops>=3`, 18 units, N4 does not; underpowered, not shown; the rejected contrast is positive, not the direction a stop rule needs). Branch B's grid (run under the as-run rejection) is re-judged on hindsight-free statistics only, with the session-matched control percentile set aside as a hindsight-biased comparator for sequential rules (section R.3: the same rule sits at its 0.0th percentile on memoryless streams). The family now holds 48 cells (16 hour-conditioned cells added for Judge 2's hour interaction, section R.4); the nested-CV OOF rule has diff -52.05 (top-1%-removed -61.27), the CPCV 5th percentile is -80.12, PBO 0.8248, SPA p 0.5965, and `harness.go_no_go` fails for the cell chosen on all IS both as computed and without its control check (failing: diff_top1_removed>0, kept_mean_slip8>0, cpcv_p5_diff>0, pbo<=0.2, dsr_p<0.1, spa_p<=0.10). The cells' pooled diffs sit at memoryless percentiles 18-80 and the within-hour kept-vs-skipped contrast's 90 % CI excludes zero on 4 of 48 cells (section R.5). The no-key conclusion of the as-run study stands; the memory claim, its direction and the "reverse rule" follow-up are withdrawn.

## R. Repair round (2026-09-29): the refuters' three issues, what changed, and the repaired result

Script `session_stop_repair.py` (runtime 5473.1 s; log `session_stop_repair.log`, `repair_run.nohup`), its pre-registration `preregistration_repair.json` (sha256 `56c45828cd02e985`, registered 2026-09-29T05:21:46, written before the first repaired statistic). Ledger sha before the repair `d475f67c4ce346ec`, after `b7a266d10a48343a`; every new ledger row carries `note = "repair"`; the as-run rows are untouched (append-only ledger). `session_stop.py` itself was not re-run; its docstring carries a dated repair note (the as-run rows' `script_sha` is `6645343d4dfba103`, the file before the note). The refuters' issues, verbatim in substance:

- **I1** the N1 rejection is a false positive of a mis-specified null (positions are generated by the outcomes; a memoryless process reproduces every reported number);
- **I2** the session-matched random control is a hindsight-biased comparator for a within-session sequential rule (`control_pct` 0.0 is not anti-edge);
- **I3** Judge 2's hour interaction was not run after the (as-run) rejection.

### R.1 Issue I1: why N1 cannot test session memory, and the memoryless demonstration

**Mechanism (real IS units vs the memoryless generator).** The generator (definitions in section 1b) keeps the real session skeleton and the clock, draws every outcome iid from the hour bin's pool, and lets the drawn unit's own duration decide when the next SETUP can occur (variant: a duration independent of the outcome). `cell_multi_*` = units in session x hour_bin cells with > 1 member (the only rows N1 can move); `last` / `nonlast` / `first` by position in the cell; `p_follow_given_*` = another unit follows in the session. content.content:
## Judges' verdicts

### Judge 1

Skeptical-practitioner verdict. The tape sets the ceiling before any model runs: 1m Foundation is +1.9 pts per trade gross against ~16 pts of cost (mean net -922 INR, 15.2% winners, 4,502 IS SETUPs in 579 active sessions); 5m is 184 IS winners with the top decile carrying ~46% of gross and an IS-to-OOS mean shift from -277 to -1,060 per trade. So any gate must find a subset whose expectancy clears ~16-20 pts, and the whole signal lives in a few hundred trades on 1m and a few dozen on 5m. On that sample the block-bootstrap CI of a kept-vs-skipped difference will be several hundred INR per trade wide; most candidates will not clear it, and that is the honest expected outcome. Every library the 18 studies name is present (sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, scipy, matplotlib) and statsmodels/torch/mapie are absent as assumed; feasibility failures are compute and memory, not imports.

Keep seven, merged into five lines of work, about 1-1.5 CPU-hours per timeframe in total: (1) one validation harness = quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's SPA, adversarial drift and 5m null tapes folded in (one ledger, one bootstrap, one PBO, active sessions only, every comparator re-priced on the L1 15:25 label); (2) one feature-vocabulary pass = quant-ml-canon-feature-importance, its 8-cluster shortlist frozen in the ledger before any gate search, with BOCPD, FFD and the novelty scalars entering there and nowhere else; (3) one learned-gate family = quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate and decision-making-1 merged (L1 label, capped |net| weights, top-1%-winners-removed as a hard pass, block-wise sign test, one distilled rule list or scorecard as the single OOS candidate from the family); (4) the interpretable candidate = deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses with a blind round 0 from the user's words alone, hashed before any table is shown, and cross-fitted round-1 tables; (5) the cheap desk rule = decision-making-6 session stop with an hour-conditioned null. That yields at most three OOS looks: the rule list from (3), the round-0 list from (4), and the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as comparator, with (5) as a multiplication if its null is rejected.

Drop or defer eleven. The sequence and representation studies (rocket, pretrain, HMM/jump, motif/shapelet, vision) share one structural flaw: the only shippable form is a depth-3 tree on the same scalar features the tabular studies already search, so they add trials to the ledger without adding a candidate, and the pre-SETUP window is templated by the engine's own SETUP definition; pretrain and 1m FQI also need 750-900 MB for hours on a box shared with another build. The two conformal studies and the two sizing studies do not change which SETUPs are taken: they choose a threshold on a score another study produces, or size a positive edge that does not yet exist; their useful pieces (slippage 3/5/8 sensitivity, Pareto front with user-chosen w, |net|-weighted coverage, one-lot-or-skip verdict) become sections of the gate study's deliverable. The regime-breaks study keeps only its break tests as the harness's pre-registration step (they decide time-decay weights and the OOS caveat); BSADF is a feature candidate for the importance pass, not a gate. The exit study is worth its parametric learner C (config keys the lab already has, 10 minutes by replay) but must be coordinated with the ST9-12 session, which already ran an exit grid on 2026.

Two standing caveats every OOS table must carry: the OOS window (2026-01-01..09-25) is also the published lab dashboard window and was used by the ST9-12 exit grid, so it is not pristine; and the 5m Foundation label as built holds 358 of 1,012 trades past the entry session, so ST13/ST14 (square_off 15:25) must be judged on the recomputed intraday label and every comparator re-priced on it.

### Judge 2

Twelve of eighteen studies are worth running here; six are cut or folded. The binding facts: (1) sample size, not compute, is the limit: 684 IS winners on 1m and 184 on 5m, a 15-22% win rate, mean net -922 INR per trade against ~1,050 INR costs, so a gate must find a subset averaging > 16 pts, and the top-decile winners are half of gross wins; every learned number must therefore be reported as a CPCV path distribution (5th percentile), with |net| weights winsorised and kept-n floors. (2) memory: lab.py holds 1.24 GB and 759 MB is free, so the '2 processes under 1 GB' budget is currently one process under ~600 MB; the rocket probe at 10k kernels, the pretrain ladder, 1m FQI and 1m synthetic tapes do not fit until lab.py exits. (3) libraries: everything named that is present imports (numpy, pandas, scipy, sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, matplotlib, PIL, joblib); statsmodels, torch, mapie, hmmlearn, ruptures, arch are absent and every study that names them correctly hand-codes. Structural fixes that apply across the set: there must be ONE harness (merge quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's bootstrap/PBO): 12 contiguous IS session blocks, purge by the label's own exit bar, 3-session embargo, one append-only ledger reached only through a score() function, PBO <= 0.2, kept-share/kept-n floors, slippage-8-pt survival, and ONE OOS script run once for at most 3 frozen candidates; all eighteen 'OOS once' clauses collapse into that, otherwise OOS is opened eighteen times. Four near-duplicate pairs merge: meta-label + policy-tree gate (the central study, EV 4), conformal-skip + conformal-risk-control (one operating-point step the user chooses on), the two sizing studies (conditional on a gate surviving; prior is 'one lot or skip'), the two harnesses. The L1 intraday (15:25) label written once is the only training label; the engine label's multi-session holds (358 of 1,012 on 5m) make purging by it too costly. Regime, novelty and state-model outputs enter as candidate features into the importance study rather than as separate gate searches, which is the cheapest cut in multiplicity. The LLM-hypothesis study needs a blind round 0 and a trials count equal to the labelled cells shown; the vision study runs as a 40-session pilot against mechanical proxies first; both must be separate agents from any study author. Cut: pretrain-probe (3-4 h, 750 MB, negative result foreseen), motif/shapelet (keep only the causal novelty score), rocket as proposed (reduce to a 5-minute ceiling check), both sizing studies as standalone. Run order: break tests and L1 label, harness, importance, merged gate, operating point, exit learners C and B (FQI on 5m only), session-stop, BOCPD/GMM regime, LLM rounds, vision pilot, null tapes on 5m; everything above 600 MB waits for lab.py.

## Designers' rationales
=====CONF
### quant-ml-canon-conformal-skip (priority 4)

**technique.** Class-conditional (Mondrian) cross-conformal prediction on the meta-model's nonconformity score, with the skip decision defined as 'win is not in the prediction set', a Mondrian taxonomy by class x time bin for the user's 'different for different time', and Adaptive Conformal Inference for drift in the live/walk-forward version.

**what_it_answers.** The user's acceptance criterion made formal: can SETUPs be skipped with a finite-sample guarantee that at most alpha of the true winners are skipped (marginally over SETUPs, under exchangeability), what skip rate, loser recall and kept-vs-skipped expectancy each alpha buys on IS out-of-fold, whether the winner coverage holds on OOS, what the hour-of-day guarantee costs in sample size, and how far a coverage-chosen threshold sits from the expectancy-chosen threshold of the meta-label study.

**method.** Score s(x) = 1 - p_win_hat(x) taken from the meta-label study's IS out-of-fold probabilities (the scorecard variant, since the forest cannot live in the lab; the forest's scores are reported as reference). Cross-conformal / CV+ flavour: no separate calibration split is sacrificed (181 winners on 5m IS cannot afford one); within the harness's 12 purged folds, the conformal quantile is computed on the OOF scores of the winners in 11 folds and applied to the 12th, so the IS evaluation is itself out-of-fold. Mondrian by class: q_alpha = the ceil((n_win + 1)(1 - alpha))-th smallest OOF score among true winners; the prediction set contains 'win' iff s(x) <= q_alpha; gate = skip iff 'win' is not in the set, i.e. p_win_hat(x) < 1 - q_alpha. Guarantee: P(win in set | true winner) >= 1 - alpha, so at most alpha of winners are skipped in expectation; nothing is guaranteed for losers, their recall is measured. Alpha grid {0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30}; the smallest feasible alpha is 1/(n_win + 1) (0.0055 on 5m IS). Time taxonomy: class x time bin with three bins fixed in advance (09:15-10:29, 10:30-12:59, 13:00-15:19; the IS hour profile shows morning losses and afternoon gains); feasibility stated from winner counts per bin (5m IS: 16-39 winners per hour, so per-bin guarantees only for alpha >= 0.1; on 1m roughly 4-5x more). Robustness: |net|-weighted coverage (share of winners' gross net kept) reported next to count coverage, because the guarantee is per SETUP, not per rupee. Evaluation on IS-OOF per alpha: skip rate, winner coverage, loser recall, kept-vs-skipped expectancy and permutation p, control percentile (fz_report.random_control), top-decile-winner coverage; alpha chosen on IS by the pre-registered rule 'largest loser recall subject to winner coverage >= 0.9 and kept-vs-skipped difference > 0'. Exchangeability check: coverage per IS year and against the regime study's break tests. ACI variant (Gibbs and Candes): alpha_t+1 = alpha_t + gamma (alpha - err_t), gamma in {0.005, 0.01}, run sequentially over IS in time order, then continued into OOS from IS's final state without re-tuning, to see whether an online alpha keeps coverage under drift. OOS once: the frozen (alpha, taxonomy, thresholds) and the frozen ACI state, same table.

**leakage_controls.** Scores are out-of-fold from the purged, embargoed splitter; the conformal quantile uses only winners from calibration folds; alpha, the time bins and the selection rule are fixed before OOS; ACI's state carries forward without any OOS tuning; the study reads no OOS row until the single frozen run; the comparison with the expectancy-chosen tau is on IS-OOF only.

**compute.** Quantiles over <= 5k scores x 5 alphas x 12 folds and a sequential ACI loop over <= 5k rows: under 1 CPU-minute, under 100 MB; it depends only on the meta-label study's OOF file.

**libraries.** numpy, pandas; mapie is not installed and not needed (split/cross-conformal quantile and ACI are about 40 lines); fz_report.random_control / permutation_p read-only.

**output_as_config.** A "conformal" block in ST13/ST14: {"alpha": 0.10, "taxonomy": "class" or "class_x_timebin", "time_bins": [["09:15","10:29"],["10:30","12:59"],["13:00","15:19"]], "skip_if_score_below": s (per bin, the deployable scorecard's score at 1 - q_alpha), "calibration": {"n_winners": n, "is_window": "2021-10-01..2025-12-31", "oof_scores_sha": ...}, "aci": {"enabled": false or true, "gamma": 0.01, "alpha_state": a}}. The lab compares the scorecard score with a number; nothing else is code. Because the threshold is a single number per bin, it is the most compact form any gate in this study set can take.

**novelty.** Vovk, Gammerman and Shafer (2005) Algorithmic Learning in a Random World; Mondrian conformal prediction (Vovk 2012); cross-conformal (Vovk 2015) and CV+ / jackknife+ (Barber, Candes, Ramdas and Tibshirani 2021, Annals of Statistics); Angelopoulos and Bates (2021) A gentle introduction to conformal prediction; Gibbs and Candes (2021) Adaptive Conformal Inference under distribution shift, NeurIPS. Current because conformal sets on top of a meta-labelling model are the 2021-2025 way to turn 'skip only losers' into a coverage statement with a finite-sample guarantee; it is not in AFML but is the natural successor to its bet-sizing chapter.

**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Trap: the guarantee is on winner count while P&L sits in the tail (a gate can keep 90% of winners and skip the three that made the year), exchangeability fails across the IS/OOS shift (5m -277 to -1,060), and the threshold it selects is the same number study 2 selects by expectancy, so it changes no trade. Fix: do not run as a study; report |net|-weighted coverage of the frozen gate as one row of study 2's OOS table; if a guarantee is ever wanted, weighted conformal on |net| with sessions as units.

**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: State the cross-conformal caveat: the OOF scores of the 11 calibration folds come from models that saw the 12th fold, so the finite-sample guarantee is the weaker CV+ / jackknife+ form (roughly 1 - 2 alpha), not 1 - alpha; report empirical OOF winner coverage per fold next to the nominal alpha. Merge with decision-making-4 into ONE operating-point step that reports both guarantees (winner coverage here, kept-loss risk there) on the same scorecard score, presents the Pareto front, and lets the user pick the point (Rule 0(c)); it is the same candidate as the scorecard for the OOS budget, not a second OOS look. Time-bin taxonomy only on 1m (5m has 16-39 winners per hour). Compute < 1 min.

=====SEL
### decision-making-4-selective-gate-conformal-risk-control (priority 4)

**technique.** Selective classification with a reject option and conformal risk control: a distribution-free finite-sample certificate on the loss of the kept trades, the winner-retained vs loser-avoided Pareto front, and cost-assumption sensitivity, to fix the gate's operating point

**what_it_answers.** Where to set the gate's threshold so that it "avoids only loss trades and not profitable ones" in a quantified, certified way: for a chosen coverage (share of SETUPs kept) what mean loss / loser share among kept trades can be guaranteed, how much winner-net is given up, and whether the chosen point survives slippage of 3 / 5 / 8 pts per side.

**method.** Score: the out-of-fold IS score from study 1 (E[net|x] or weighted P(win)). (i) Selective risk-coverage curves on IS CV: coverage c in [0.1, 1.0], selective risk = mean of clipped loss L = min(max(-net, 0), 6,000 INR) among kept, and separately the loser share; the curve is the decision surface the user chooses on. (ii) Conformal Risk Control (Angelopoulos, Bates, Candes, Jordan & Lei 2022): split IS by session blocks into train (for the score) and a calibration block (>= 200 sessions); for a target risk alpha, pick the largest coverage lambda whose calibration risk (with the +B/(n+1) correction, B = the clip) is <= alpha; the guarantee E[risk of kept] <= alpha holds under exchangeability of calibration units, which here are sessions (aggregate to session-level losses so weak dependence within a day does not break the units); report alpha in {800, 1,000, 1,200 INR} (the cost level: 1m mean cost 1,048-1,116 INR). (iii) Cost-aware operating point: utility U_w = sum kept net - w * sum over skipped of max(net, 0) for w in {0, 0.5, 1}; the Pareto front (winner-net retained %, loser-net avoided %) is presented and the user picks w (Rule 0(c): the operating point is a user decision, not a fit). (iv) Sensitivity: recompute every net at slippage 3 / 5 / 8 pts per side and with the brokerage cap at 20 vs 0.03% uncapped; the chosen point must keep a positive kept-minus-skipped difference at 8 pts. OOS once: realised selective risk vs the certified alpha (does the certificate hold?), kept share vs the planned coverage, kept/skipped expectancy, control percentile.

**leakage_controls.** Scores come from out-of-fold IS predictions only (never in-sample fits); the calibration block is disjoint in time from the score's training folds and sits after them with a 2-session embargo; the clip B and the risk definition are fixed above; w is chosen by the user on IS curves before OOS is opened; OOS is evaluated once at the frozen (lambda, w).

**compute.** Seconds to a few minutes: numpy sweeps over <= 5k rows, 2,000 control draws, four slippage variants.

**libraries.** numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn 1.7.2 (calibration utilities), matplotlib for the risk-coverage plot in the report

**output_as_config.** strategy_13/14.json "gate" additions: {"operating_point": {"coverage": lambda, "min_expected_net_inr": tau_at_lambda, "certified_risk_inr": alpha, "clip_inr": 6000, "calibration_sessions": n, "winner_weight_w": w}, "cost_assumptions": {"slippage_pts_per_side": 5, "survives_slippage_pts": 8}} with provenance. The certificate numbers are documentation of the guarantee, the two thresholds are the only trading numbers.

**novelty.** Chow 1970 (reject option) and Geifman & El-Yaniv 2017 (selective classification, risk-coverage) frame skip as abstention with a known zero cost; Angelopoulos et al. 2022 (Conformal Risk Control) and Bates et al. 2021 (RCPS) give the finite-sample guarantee that a plain threshold on a GBM score does not; the cost-aware utility follows the risk-sensitive decision literature (Rockafellar & Uryasev 2000 CVaR as the alternative risk if the user prefers tail control to mean loss). This is the study that turns the user's sentence about bands into a number with a guarantee attached.

**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Trap: a certificate under session exchangeability that the 5m IS-to-OOS shift already violates; it sets a threshold on study 13's score, it is not a gate, and it would consume one of the three OOS slots for a re-parameterisation. Fix: the risk-coverage curve, the 3/5/8-pt slippage sensitivity, the brokerage-cap variant and the user-chosen w become one section of study 13's deliverable (Rule 0(c): the operating point is the user's decision on IS curves); drop the CRC certificate or footnote it with the exchangeability caveat.

**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: Merge with quant-ml-canon-conformal-skip into one operating-point step on the same OOF score: report winner coverage (that study) and certified kept-loss risk (this one) on one Pareto front, and let the user pick w and the coverage on IS curves before OOS; one candidate, one OOS look. The calibration block of >= 200 sessions holds only ~110 sessions with a SETUP on 1m and fewer on 5m: state n as sessions-with-SETUPs and the resulting B/(n+1) slack, and drop the per-bin certificate on 5m. Keep the slippage 3/5/8 pts and brokerage-cap sensitivity as a mandatory harness go/no-go item for every gate (a marginal gate must survive 8 pts).

## 6. Why sequential reinforcement learning is not used here

The decision is one step per SETUP: take or skip at the SETUP bar. Foundation took every SETUP, so the reward of `take` (the L1 net) is observed for every context and the reward of `skip` is 0 by definition: the counterfactual is in the table, no arm is unobserved, no propensity model, no inverse-propensity weighting and no doubly-robust correction is needed (Dudik-Langford-Li's estimator collapses to the direct method), and the off-policy value of any gate is exact: sum over SETUPs of pi(x) x net(x). On L1 no two positions overlap by construction (average uniqueness 1.0 on the IS rows, logged in `run_<tf>_<sub>.log`), the next SETUP needs the CHoCH that exits the previous trade, and the 15:25 cut ends every position inside its session, so no state carries from one decision to the next: there is no return to bootstrap, no credit assignment across decisions and nothing a sequential learner (Q-learning, policy gradient, FQI) could exploit that supervised meta-labelling / a full-information contextual bandit does not already compute exactly. Sequential RL is justified only where today's action changes which future rewards remain reachable (the in-trade exit, studied in `exit_policy` as an Exo-MDP with FQI: no exit variant rescued the book; and the session-level stop, studied in `session_stop`: null). The 'generative' element the canon endorses at this sample size is the CPCV path distribution and the stationary block bootstrap of sessions (the harness), and the null tapes of `null_tapes_drift`.

## 7. What would falsify these findings

- A rule-list or scorecard form with a nested CPCV 5th percentile > 0, PBO <= 0.2 over the family, DSR p < 0.1 with n_trials = the family size, SPA p <= 0.10, a bootstrap 90% CI of the diff above 0, kept share >= 20%, kept n >= 300 / 80, diff > 0 with the top 1% winners removed, kept mean > 0 at 8 pts slippage, diff > 0 in >= 8 of 12 blocks, control percentile >= 95, AND a real-tape diff above the GMM-Markov and segment-bootstrap p95 of its own null tapes: the finalist-set tables show which items fail for every form.
- A ceiling model with an OOF AUC materially above 0.59 (1 min) / 0.50 (5 min) on this table: the importance study's bagging and this study's HGB (b) are the two gradient / bagged ceilings and both sit there.
- A tau grid on which the nested recall constraint (|net|-weighted winner recall >= 0.90) is met by a threshold above the floor in most folds: the 'tau constraint met' column shows how often the constraint bound at the floor.

## 8. Caveats

- The shortlist is empty on both timeframes; sub-family (II) is H5 on the whole as-of table and is OUTSIDE THE FROZEN SHORTLIST in every row; its multiplicity is counted in the same family as (I).
- Every HGB fit bins with unweighted quantiles (sklearn < 1.7 behaviour) because sklearn 1.9's weighted bin mapper costs ~25 s per fit; the study weights enter the loss unchanged.
- The fixed-tau, time-decay, structural-sensitivity and robustness-label rows are scored with controls off (they are trials, never candidates); their vectors are in the family for PBO / SPA.
- The frozen rule list distilled from the pooled OOF decisions and the scorecard / policy learner refit on all IS are in-sample selections (one trial each); the candidate rule judges the NESTED forms (their own OOF row and CPCV distribution), as both judges asked.
- The policy learners carry the DM-1 kept-share floor (>= 20% of the training rows) inside the search: without it the value-maximising tree skips every SETUP because the book's expectancy is negative in every hour x direction cell.
- A rule on an ext-features column (features_ext) is expressible on the real tape but cannot be replayed on the null tapes (their feature tables carry the 261 base columns): the null-tape item then reads 'not evaluable' and the form cannot be a candidate.
- `sl` and `n_events_asof` (drift.json time proxies) are excluded from sub-family (II); the interaction pairs that carry them are unusable and are listed.
- Two processes appended to the ledger concurrently (procA: 5minute context / 5minute h5_full / minute context; procB / procB2: minute h5_full; procC / procD: the 5minute scorecard and 5minute h5_full reruns with jobs=1); every line was parsed back by finalize (ids unique per config).
- The minute / context run (procA) was killed with its agent at 14:03 UTC during the hgbc robustness stage (L0 fold 4 of 12; no ledger row of that stage had been written: the stage scores after its 12 folds). It was restarted at 15:35 UTC (procA2.nohup, GF_JOBS=4) from its checkpoints: bag4 (all stages) and hgbc (oof12, cpcv, frozen) were not rerun; hgbc robust, hgbr, pt1-pt3, scorecard and diag ran in the restart. Every model is seeded (random_state 0 / per-estimator seeds), so the job count changes timings only.
- On 5minute the scorecard's C-search was run twice: the first runs walked the C grid linearly (`c_search = linear`; results kept as `scorecard_linear.pkl`, its rows are separate trials in the ledger because `c_search` is part of the config), the rerun bisects (`bisect`, `scorecard.pkl`, the procedure every other (tf, sub) uses). Both are in the family; the bisect one is the reported scorecard.
- The L3 label is dimensionless (a t-value); its rows' slippage column is not read; the L2 labels use the engine's same-bar conventions and are checked against the L1 stop exits.
- IS/OOS: no OOS row was read; the OOS window is the published lab window (BRIEF caveat).

"""Evaluate gates on a synthetic null tape's own feature table (study null_tapes_drift; DESIGN_PANEL decision-making-3 (c)).

A tape folder is what build.py --path <tape.csv> --out <folder> wrote: features.parquet, trades.parquet, sessions.parquet,
bars.parquet, events.parquet, setups.parquet, meta.json. Nothing here touches OUT/ledger: tape results stay in the study
folder (the ledger is for the real tape only).

    import tapes
    T = tapes.load_tape(folder)                       # a harness.Table over the tape's L1 units (all rows are IS by construction)
    res = tapes.evaluate_rule_list(folder, rules)     # rules: a rule-list JSON (grammar below) -> kept-vs-skipped diff, control pct, ...
    res = tapes.evaluate_keep(T, keep_mask, tag)      # any boolean keep mask through harness.metrics (2,000-draw controls)
    h = tapes.tape_health(folder)                     # the engine-health check of one tape (lock-out share, SETUP rate vs real, healthy flag)
    tapes.tape_folders(tf, gen)                       # the CERTIFICATE tape set: the first DESIGN_N healthy tapes per generator (healthy=False: every tape built)
    tapes.null_tape_check(real_diff, tf, rules)       # the pass rule of FINDINGS section 7 as go_no_go-shaped items

Rule-list grammar (the one the LLM-hypothesis study uses, rules_round0.json): a list of rules, each
    {"if": [[column, op, value], ...] (at most 3 comparisons, conjunction), "then": "skip"}
over as-of columns of features.parquet; ops >=, >, <=, <, ==, !=, in, not_in. A SETUP is skipped when ANY rule fires
(disjunction of conjunctions); NaN never satisfies a comparison. A dict {"rules": [...]} or {"minute": [...], "5minute": [...]}
is accepted too (the timeframe list is picked by the tape's tf). A rule may carry "then": "keep" — then the listed rules are
the KEEP set (a SETUP is kept when any keep rule fires); mixing keep and skip rules in one list is refused.

Refused columns (PermissionError): label columns (harness.LABEL_PREFIX), harness.NOT_FEATURES (fz_traded, raw prices, ids), and
the calendar proxies drift.py found (|Spearman rho| >= 0.9 with session_idx: `n_events_asof`, `sl`; read from drift.json,
TIME_PROXIES_FALLBACK when the file is missing). A rule on a time proxy is a calendar rule, not a market rule (FINDINGS section 6).

Engine health of a tape (repair round): on a driftless random-walk tape the engine's protected level can freeze — the anchored
AVWAP of the last flip lags a long one-directional walk, no new swing qualifies as a protected-level candidate (engine.qualifies:
a low below / a high above that AVWAP), `prot` stays at the last candidate and a CHoCH (a close beyond `prot` against the trend)
becomes unreachable while BOS continues. Sessions inside a frozen-`prot`, CHoCH-free run longer than the real tape's longest such
run (68 / 69 sessions on 5minute / minute) are counted as dead; a tape is HEALTHY when its dead share is < HEALTH["dead_share_max"]
(0.2) AND its SETUP rate is >= HEALTH["setup_rate_ratio_min"] (1/3) x the real tape's. The health flag never reads a label or a
gate statistic. The certificate (null_distributions.json `gates`, FINDINGS section 4) is read on the first DESIGN_N healthy
tapes per generator (by seed index k); the sets with the locked tapes are published beside it (`gates_all_original`,
`gates_healthy_original`).

How a candidate is evaluated on the tapes later: for every tape folder of tape_folders(tf, gen) (the certificate set),
evaluate_rule_list(folder, rules) gives the tape's diff and control percentile; the candidate's real-tape diff (its ledger row)
is compared with the p95 of the tape diffs per generator: it passes the null-tape check when its real-tape diff is above the
GMM-Markov p95 AND above the segment p95, and its session-bootstrap diffs are of the same sign as the real one in at least 75%
of the certificate session tapes (null_tape_check does exactly this; see FINDINGS.md section 7).
"""
import os, sys, json, glob
sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))
if OUT not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, OUT)
import harness as H                                                     # noqa: E402

MECHANICAL_GATES = {
    "frozen_st7_st8": "keep = fz_traded (the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as traded on the tape)",
    "choch2_skip": "skip when n_choch_since_bos >= 2 (mechanical reference gate 1: fixed in tapes.py before any tape was scored; a reference point, not a candidate; BRIEF H2 names the family without k)",
    "sl_above_median_skip": "skip when sl_dist_atr > the tape's own IS median of sl_dist_atr (mechanical reference gate 2: fixed in tapes.py before any tape was scored; a reference point, not a candidate)",

def rules_for(rules, tf):
    if isinstance(rules, dict):
        if "rules" in rules: rules = rules["rules"]
        elif tf in rules: rules = rules[tf]
        else: raise ValueError("rule JSON needs 'rules' or a per-timeframe list")
    return list(rules)


def rule_mask(F, rules, tf):
    """(fires, mode): fires[i] = any rule's conjunction holds on row i; mode = 'skip' or 'keep'.
    Refuses (PermissionError) a label column, a harness.NOT_FEATURES column and a calendar proxy (time_proxies(tf))."""
    rules = rules_for(rules, tf)
    modes = {str(r.get("then", "skip")).lower() for r in rules}
    if len(modes) > 1: raise ValueError(f"a rule list mixes {sorted(modes)}; use one mode")
    mode = modes.pop() if modes else "skip"
    proxies = time_proxies(tf)
    fires = np.zeros(len(F), dtype=bool)
    for r in rules:
        conds = r["if"]
        if len(conds) > 3: raise ValueError(f"rule {r.get('id')} has depth {len(conds)} > 3")
        m = np.ones(len(F), dtype=bool)
        for col, op, val in conds:
            if col not in F.columns: raise KeyError(f"rule {r.get('id')}: column {col} not in the feature table")
            if col.startswith(H.LABEL_PREFIX) or col in H.NOT_FEATURES: raise PermissionError(f"rule {r.get('id')}: {col} is not an as-of feature")
            if col in proxies: raise PermissionError(f"rule {r.get('id')}: {col} is a time proxy (drift.json time_proxies, |rho| >= 0.9 with session_idx): a calendar rule, refused")
            m &= _cmp(F[col], op, val)
        fires |= m
    return fires, mode

def _tape_k(folder):

def _frozen_runs(folder):
    """Per IS session: prot frozen (no change inside the session and equal to the previous session's last prot) and no CHoCH.
    Returns (n_sessions, run lengths of consecutive frozen sessions, per-session frozen flags, position of the last CHoCH session,
    the longest CHoCH-free stretch in sessions, the session dates)."""
    B = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(folder, "bars.parquet"), columns=["i", "session_idx", "close", "prot", "split"])
    if "split" in B.columns: B = B[B.split.astype(str) == "IS"]
    E = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(folder, "events.parquet"), columns=["i", "kind"])
    S = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(folder, "sessions.parquet"))
    S = S[S.split.astype(str) == "IS"].sort_values("session_idx")
    sess = S.session_idx.to_numpy(); n_s = len(sess); pos = {int(s): j for j, s in enumerate(sess)}
    pr = B.prot.fillna(-1.0)
    g = pd.DataFrame(dict(session_idx=B.session_idx.to_numpy(), prot=pr.to_numpy())).groupby("session_idx").prot.agg(["first", "last", "nunique"])
    g = g.reindex(sess)
    prev_last = g["last"].shift(1)
    moved = (g["nunique"] > 1) | (g["first"] != prev_last)
    moved.iloc[0] = True
    b2s = dict(zip(B.i.to_numpy(), B.session_idx.to_numpy()))
    ch_sess = {b2s[i] for i in E[E.kind == "CHoCH"].i.to_numpy() if i in b2s}
    has_ch = np.array([s in ch_sess for s in sess])
    frozen = ~(moved.to_numpy() | has_ch)
    runs = []; c = 0
    for v in frozen:
        if v: c += 1
        elif c: runs.append(c); c = 0
    if c: runs.append(c)
    ch_pos = sorted(pos[s] for s in ch_sess)
    last_ch = ch_pos[-1] if ch_pos else -1
    stretches = np.diff(np.array([-1] + ch_pos + [n_s])) - 1
    return dict(n_sessions=int(n_s), runs=np.array(runs, dtype=int) if runs else np.zeros(0, dtype=int), frozen=frozen, last_choch_pos=int(last_ch),
                longest_choch_free=int(stretches.max()) if len(stretches) else int(n_s), dates=S.date.astype(str).to_numpy(),
                prot_last=(None if np.isnan(B.prot.iloc[-1]) else float(B.prot.iloc[-1])), close_last=float(B.close.iloc[-1]), is_bar_ids=set(B.i.tolist()))

def tape_health(folder, real=None, write=True):

    longer than the real tape's longest such run; healthy = dead share < HEALTH['dead_share_max'] and SETUP rate >=
    HEALTH['setup_rate_ratio_min'] x real. Writes tape_health.json into the folder (write=True). Reads no label."""

               longest_frozen_run_start=(fr["dates"][start] if start is not None else None),
               dead_sessions=dead, dead_share=round(dead_share, 4), dead_runs=[int(x) for x in dead_runs],
               dead_tail_share=round((n_s - 1 - fr["last_choch_pos"]) / n_s, 4), longest_choch_free_sessions=fr["longest_choch_free"],
               last_choch_date=(fr["dates"][fr["last_choch_pos"]] if fr["last_choch_pos"] >= 0 else None),
               last_setup_time=(str(P.time.max()) if len(P) else None), setups=int(len(P)), setups_per_session=round(setups_ps, 4),
               setup_rate_ratio_to_real=(round(ratio, 4) if ratio is not None else None), prot_last=fr["prot_last"], close_last=fr["close_last"],
               prot_gap_pts=(round(fr["close_last"] - fr["prot_last"], 2) if fr["prot_last"] is not None else None),
               real_longest_frozen_run_sessions=L, real_setups_per_session=real["setups_per_session"],
               healthy=(len(reasons) == 0), reasons=reasons, rule=dict(HEALTH, dead_run_longer_than=L))
    if write:

    return out


def read_health(folder, compute=True):
    p = os.path.join(folder, "tape_health.json")
    if os.path.exists(p): return json.load(open(p, encoding="utf-8"))
    return tape_health(folder) if compute else None


def all_tape_folders(tf, gen=None):
    """Every built tape folder of the timeframe (and generator), sorted by generator then seed index k (numeric)."""
    pat = os.path.join(HERE, "tapes", tf, f"{gen or '*'}_*")
    fs = [p for p in glob.glob(pat) if os.path.exists(os.path.join(p, "features.parquet"))]
    return sorted(fs, key=lambda p: (_tape_gen(p), _tape_k(p)))


def tape_folders(tf, gen=None, healthy=True, n=None, original_only=False):
    """The tape set a candidate is evaluated on.
    healthy=True (default, the CERTIFICATE set): per generator the first n (= DESIGN_N[tf]) tapes by seed index k whose
    tape_health.json says healthy (computed when missing). healthy=False: every tape built (n=None) or the first n per generator.
    original_only=True restricts to k < DESIGN_N[tf] (the tapes of the first build, locked ones included when healthy=False)."""
    n = DESIGN_N[tf] if n is None and healthy else n
    out = []
    for g in sorted({_tape_gen(p) for p in all_tape_folders(tf, gen)}):
        fs = all_tape_folders(tf, g)

        if healthy: fs = [p for p in fs if read_health(p)["healthy"]]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the pass rule (FINDINGS section 7) as go_no_go-shaped items
def null_tape_check_from_diffs(real_diff, diffs, session_same_sign_min=PASS_RULE["session_same_sign_min"]):
    """diffs = {'gmm': [...], 'segment': [...], 'session': [...]} (one diff per certificate tape). Returns (passed, checks, summary):
    checks are (ok, value) pairs like harness.go_no_go's; passed = real diff > gmm p95 AND > segment p95 AND the session tapes
    carry the real sign in >= 75% of tapes."""
    q = lambda v, p: (round(float(np.nanquantile(v, p)), 2) if len(v) and np.isfinite(v).any() else None)
    ch, summ = {}, {}
    for g in ("gmm", "segment"):
        v = np.asarray(diffs.get(g, []), dtype=float); p95 = q(v, 0.95)
        ch[f"null_tape:real_diff>{g}_p95"] = (real_diff is not None and p95 is not None and real_diff > p95, p95)
        summ[g] = dict(n=int(len(v)), p50=q(v, 0.5), p95=q(v, 0.95), real_pct=(round(float(100 * np.nanmean(v < real_diff)), 1) if len(v) and real_diff is not None else None))
    v = np.asarray(diffs.get("session", []), dtype=float)
    same = float(np.nanmean(np.sign(v) == np.sign(real_diff))) if len(v) and real_diff is not None else None
    ch[f"null_tape:session_same_sign>={session_same_sign_min}"] = (same is not None and same >= session_same_sign_min, round(same, 3) if same is not None else None)
    summ["session"] = dict(n=int(len(v)), p50=q(v, 0.5), p95=q(v, 0.95), same_sign_share=(round(same, 3) if same is not None else None))
    summ["null_tape_diff_inr"] = {g: {"p50": summ[g]["p50"], "p95": summ[g]["p95"]} for g in ("gmm", "segment", "session") if g in summ}
    return all(v[0] for v in ch.values()), ch, summ

    healthy, the design count per generator), compare the real-tape diff (the candidate's ledger row) with the gmm / segment p95
    and the session sign share. Returns (passed, checks, summary); summary['per_tape'] holds every tape's result. Tape numbers
    never enter the ledger. Call it only after the candidate's real-tape ledger row exists (the tapes are not a search space)."""
    per, diffs = [], {}
    for g in ("gmm", "segment", "session"):
        diffs[g] = []
        for folder in tape_folders(tf, g):
            r = evaluate_rule_list(folder, rules, controls=controls, draws=draws, label=label)
            r.update(gen=g, k=_tape_k(folder)); per.append(r); diffs[g].append(np.nan if r["diff"] is None else r["diff"])
            if verbose: print(f"  {g}_{r['k']}: diff {r['diff']} kept_share {r['kept_share']}", flush=True)
    passed, ch, summ = null_tape_check_from_diffs(real_diff, diffs)
    summ.update(tf=tf, real_diff=real_diff, per_tape=per, tape_set="certificate (healthy, first DESIGN_N per generator)")
    return passed, ch, summ


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- reality check of a tape (or of the real IS tape)
def bar_stats(bars, sessions=None, is_only=True):
    """Per-bar within-session log-return std (bps), excess kurtosis, autocorrelation of |r| at lags 1-5 (pairs inside a session),
    the price level range and the median ATR14."""
    B = bars
    if is_only and "split" in B.columns: B = B[B.split.astype(str) == "IS"]
    B = B.sort_values("i") if "i" in B.columns else B
    c = B.close.to_numpy(dtype=float); s = B.session_idx.to_numpy()
    same = s[1:] == s[:-1]
    r = np.log(c[1:] / c[:-1])[same]                                     # within-session close-to-close returns
    ss = s[1:][same]
    out = dict(bars=int(len(B)), ret_std_bps=round(float(r.std() * 1e4), 3), ret_kurt_excess=round(float(pd.Series(r).kurt()), 3),
               ret_mean_bps=round(float(r.mean() * 1e4), 4))
    a = np.abs(r) - np.abs(r).mean()
    for lag in range(1, 6):
        m = ss[lag:] == ss[:-lag]
        x, y = a[lag:][m], a[:-lag][m]
        out[f"absret_ac{lag}"] = round(float((x * y).mean() / (a.var() + 1e-18)), 4)
    out.update(close_min=float(c.min()), close_max=float(c.max()), close_first=float(c[0]), close_last=float(c[-1]),
               atr14_median=round(float(B.atr14.median()), 3) if "atr14" in B.columns else None,
               volume_mean=round(float(B.volume.mean()), 1), zero_volume_bars=int((B.volume == 0).sum()))
    return out

    S = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(folder, "sessions.parquet")); E = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(folder, "events.parquet"))
